title: create-architectural-decision-record Review: A Solid ADR Template in Copilot Prompt Syntax
description: We used GitHub's ADR skill to record a decision our site made months ago. The template made the agent cover alternatives and downsides. The skill is a Copilot prompt file underneath, and it does not ask for evidence.

author.name: TrustedSkills Team
author.bio: We assess AI agent skills by installing them, running them against real work, and reading the source. We don't accept payment for reviews.

basisNote: Part of a batch of twelve documentation skills run on the same day against the same codebase: the TrustedSkills website repo, a Next.js 16 app. Each run worked in its own private copy of the repo. One run on one codebase is one data point, not a benchmark.

runs.task: Write an ADR for a decision the project had already made: related skills were switched off on skill detail pages. Rebuild the context, options and consequences from the code, CLAUDE.md and git history, and mark anything inferred.
runs.outcome:
`npx skills add github/awesome-copilot --skill create-architectural-decision-record` installed it first time.

The skill is a 97-line template: front matter, Status, Context, Decision, positive and negative Consequences, Alternatives with rejection reasons, Implementation Notes and References, with coded bullets such as POS-001 and ALT-002. It says to save the file as `docs/adr/adr-NNNN-<slug>.md`. The agent did, and wrote a 181-line ADR.

The agent traced the decision to a March 2026 commit that removed the related-skills grid right after the site started pre-rendering 5,000 pages. It also found that the commit's own comment said related skills would still show on pre-rendered pages, while the code turned them off everywhere. We checked both in the git history. It also found that our CLAUDE.md still describes a `related = []` line that a later commit deleted. That is correct: the line is gone and the note is stale.

The inputs are written as `${input:DecisionTitle}` and `${input:Context}`, which is GitHub Copilot prompt-file syntax. Claude Code does not fill them, so the agent took them from the task. The template defaults the status to Proposed; the agent set Accepted, since the decision had shipped.

The skill does not ask for sources. Every "why" in our ADR cites a commit or is marked inferred because our task asked for that. Six points ended up marked inferred.
runs.environment: Claude Code subagent (Sonnet 5) with the installed SKILL.md loaded as its instructions, in a private clone of the TrustedSkills website repo at commit c7e2736.

summary: A clear, standard ADR template. It makes the agent write down alternatives, why they lost, and the downsides of the choice, which are the parts people skip. On our repo it produced a useful record of an old decision and surfaced a stale note in our own agent instructions. It is a GitHub Copilot prompt file with `${input:...}` placeholders, and it has no rule that the context must come from evidence, so add that rule yourself when you are documenting a past decision.

strengths.title: Covers the parts people skip
strengths.body: Negative consequences and rejected alternatives are required sections. Our ADR listed four downsides and three alternatives.

strengths.title: Fixed location and naming
strengths.body: `docs/adr/adr-NNNN-<slug>.md` with sequential numbers. A second ADR lands next to the first without anyone deciding where it goes.

limitations.title: Copilot prompt syntax
limitations.body: Inputs are `${input:...}` variables that Copilot fills from a form. In Claude Code nothing fills them; the agent has to work them out or ask.

limitations.title: No evidence rule
limitations.body: Nothing asks where the context came from. For a decision made months ago, that is where an agent can fill gaps with guesses. Our task added the rule.

limitations.title: Coded bullets add noise
limitations.body: Every bullet gets a code like POS-001 or IMP-003. That helps machine parsing, but makes a short ADR harder for a person to read.

limitations.title: Not recently maintained
limitations.body: The skill's folder was last changed in February 2026.

bestFor.title: Recording a decision as you make it
bestFor.body: When the context is fresh, the template is all you need.

notFor: Reconstructing old decisions, unless you add your own rule that every reason must cite a commit or a file.
